findings.title: All app imports are started eagerly
findings.body: Each `import()` is evaluated while this object is constructed, so importing `@calcom/app-store` starts loading every app package rather than loading only the requested app. This defeats the intended on-demand loading and means consumers such as `videoClient` still incur the initialization and memory cost of the entire app store.

findings.title: Recurring calendar deletions are not awaited or collected
findings.body: This async `forEach` pauses at `await getCalendar()` before pushing deletions into `apiDeletes`. The handler later awaits `Promise.all(apiDeletes)`, but in this recurring-booking branch that runs before these callbacks resume, so it sees an empty array and can return without waiting for any calendar event deletion. A cancellation can therefore be reported as complete while recurring events remain on connected calendars.

findings.title: Reschedule calendar deletions run unawaited
findings.body: The async callbacks are not awaited by `forEach`. They pause at `await getCalendar()` before initiating `deleteEvent`, while the mutation proceeds to send the reschedule email and return. The request can finish before calendar deletion even starts, and failures from the callbacks are not propagated to the mutation.

findings.title: Calendar deletion callbacks are not awaited
findings.body: This async `forEach` callback waits for the dynamic calendar import, but the enclosing function does not await the callback promises. It can send the reschedule email and return before calendar deletion is initiated; callback failures also bypass the surrounding `try/catch`.
